http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27932.text: Big News Network.com "Very productive meeting," Slovak FM Juraj Blanar hails India-Visegard cooperation; highlights tech, defence cooperation New York [US], September 22 (ANI): India and the Visegrad Group (V4) countries, comprising Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, called for a pragmatic approach to energy security and diversification while highlighting opportunities for greater cooperation in defence, technology and innovation during the first V4+India Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New York, according a statement from the Slovak foreign Ministry. The meeting was held on Monday on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly under the Slovak Presidency of the V4. The meeting was chaired by Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar and attended by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orbanova, Czech Foreign Minister Petr Macinka and Polish Foreign Minister Radosaw Sikorski. Energy security and the impact of global conflicts on supply chains featured prominently in the discussions. Blanar said India and the V4 countries face challenges linked to energy security and that cooperation on the issue remains important amid global market shifts. 'I am personally pleased that we had the opportunity to exchange information regarding energy security, because India, Europe, and the V4 nations all face immense challenges related to the war in Ukraine and in the Middle East. These issues exert a profound impact on our economies, and we seek to cooperate with India in this domain as well,' Blanar said. The Slovak side also highlighted the importance of a pragmatic and non-ideological approach to energy issues, with a focus on economic and industrial competitiveness. Defence and technology cooperation also emerged as key areas for India and the V4 countries. Jaishankar described the meeting as a productive opportunity to work with the Central European group, highlighting their industrial, innovation and technological capabilities. 'It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion. It was a very, very productive meeting. These are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. These are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent, and I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide, but we certainly welcome the opportunity to work with the V4 together,' Jaishankar said. He also said India would explore greater cooperation in technology and innovation and highlighted the existing defence relationship with all four V4 countries. 'We would also explore technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defence. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation,' Jaishankar added. The discussions also covered major global developments, including the Ukraine conflict and developments in the Gulf. 'Discussions focused on cooperation as well as major global crises, including the Ukraine conflict and developments in the Gulf. It was really a very, very worthwhile, very productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it,' Jaishankar said. The meeting marked the launch of the V4+India format at the Foreign Ministers' level, providing a structured platform for India and the four Central European countries to discuss economic and strategic cooperation. Blanar said the first V4+India meeting was the result of an 11-year effort by Slovakia to establish the format and described the platform as offering strategic potential for cooperation. 'This historically first meeting organised in the V4+ India format is the result of an 11-year effort by the Slovak Republic. We did our utmost to make this meeting happen because we see strategic potential in it. I consider this session to be a historic success for Slovak diplomacy, through which we have managed to secure another major external partner for V4 cooperation,' Blanar said. The two sides also discussed economic cooperation and the potential for stronger trade and investment ties. Blanar highlighted the significance of the EU-India Free Trade Agreement and said it would create opportunities for the European Union and V4 economies. 'If everything proceeds as prepared - as Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar informed us - the EU-India Free Trade Agreement should be signed sometime in December this year. This is a major step forward, because India today stands as the fifth-largest economy and is becoming a powerful economic heavyweight. It represents a vast opportunity for the European Union, and by extension, for the states of the Visegrad Group,' Blanar said. The meeting also covered multilateral issues, including reform of the United Nations system. Slovakia reiterated its support for India's ambition to secure a permanent seat on a reformed UN Security Council, while Slovakia and India confirmed mutual support for their respective candidatures for non-permanent seats for the 2028-2029 term. The inaugural V4+India meeting thus brought energy security, defence, technology, trade and multilateral cooperation into a single framework for engagement between India and the Visegrad countries. Photograph: Lukas Coch/EPA Anthony Albanese Anthony Albanese defies critics for Apec summit photo with Vladimir Putin Despite pleas from pro-Ukraine Australians, the prime minister accepts wishes of Chinese hosts with group picture Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Tom McIlroy in Shenzhen Wed 18 Nov 2026 10.39 EST First published on Wed 18 Nov 2026 08.04 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Anthony Albanese has appeared in a leaders’ photo with Vladimir Putin at the Apec summit in China, despite Australia’s Ukrainian community urging the prime minister to protest against Russia’s war. After arriving in the Chinese tech capital, Shenzhen, on Wednesday, Albanese said he would respect the wishes of China as the hosts of this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and take part in the photo. Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up? Read more He appeared in a group shot that included Putin, the US president, Donald Trump, and China’s Xi Jinping at the summit banquet on Wednesday night. The traditional leaders’ “family photo” is due to be taken on Thursday morning. “I will bear in mind the wishes of our host,” Albanese said before the event. “China are our host here, I respect that, but we also make our position very clear when it comes to Ukraine.” Other leaders including Canada’s Mark Carney said they would take part, despite foreign affairs ministers at this month’s G20 talks in the United States refusing to pose with Russia’s Sergei Lavrov. It is the first time Putin has had a place at the forefront of a grouping of world leaders in nearly a decade. A professor of international law at Australian National University, Don Rothwell, said posing with Putin risked undermining trust in the international criminal court, where the Russian has been indicted as a war criminal over his invasion of Ukraine and the four-year war. “For the Australian prime minister to appear in a photograph with Vladimir Putin is not consistent with the international values Australia is seeking to espouse,” Rothwell told Guardian Australia. The Australian Federation of Ukrainian Organisations chairwoman, Kateryna Argyrou, had urged Albanese to boycott the event. “Vladimir Putin is not just another world leader attending an international summit,” Argyrou said. “He is an indicted war criminal and the architect of a brutal war against Ukraine – a war that has brought death, destruction and unimaginable suffering to millions of people.” China is the latest stop on Albanese’s intense diplomatic tour. View image in fullscreen Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the Apec summit. Photograph: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press/AP After Quad leaders’ talks in Manila on Tuesday night, the prime minister attended a business event and toured a supermarket selling Australian-made products in Shenzhen. The city – known as a major hub for electronics, drones and companies including Huawei and electric vehicle brand BYD – is seeing intense security as world leaders gather. Many of the streets have been cleared of local residents, allowing motorcades speedy access to the summit hubs and nearby luxury hotels. Spruiking investment in Australia, Albanese recalled first visiting Shenzhen in the 1990s and said AI could help bridge economic divides and allow for sustainable growth in the region. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Politics, really Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you after newsletter promotion “The economic potential and opportunity of artificial intelligence is enormous,” he said. “Not just for the Asia Pacific, but for the world.” As well as the main summit, Albanese will take part in bilateral meetings on Thursday, including with Mexico’s president, Claudia Sheinbaum. He will attend a lunch with Carney and the leaders of Singapore and New Zealand. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here But the trilateral talks with Trump, Xi and Putin on Thursday are set to dominate conversations in Shenzhen and in capitals around the world. Already likened to the Yalta summit after the second world war, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, warned against decisions about his country’s future being made without him. Albanese will make a diplomatic call on Xi on Friday, before a meeting in Beijing with the Chinese premier, Li Qiang. On the agenda with both leaders is a push for China to remove 55% tariffs for Australian beef exports, imposed after the country hit an annual quota for sales. Albanese said he would lobby in Australia’s interests. “Of course we’d rather not have any quotas on Australian goods anywhere in the world, but the fact they’ve hit it is a signal that Chinese consumers want to buy Australian beef because of its quality.” He said he would raise trade issues as the federal government works to stabilise trade with China after Beijing imposed a major diplomatic freeze on Australia during the former Coalition government. Albanese praised Xi’s engagement and knowledge of Australia, noting the Chinese leader had visited every state and territory.
